transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up a spot from someone who needs it more, but my wife really wanted me to come in. 

I guess the main thing is that I've just... I kind of stopped caring about everything I usually look forward to. I mean, I have a good life, I really do, so I feel a little guilty even complaining about it. But my fishing gear is just sitting untouched out in the garage, and... well, going out to the woodshop just feels like a chore lately. 

Even when my kids try to get me to play chess, I'm... I'm really just going through the motions. I feel terrible admitting that out loud, about my own kids. I just don't have the energy for it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay for you.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... it's been a little while, I guess. I kept thinking I could just snap out of it, you know? I didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But if I really think about it, it's been... probably about a year and seven months? Give or take. 

It started right around the time my wife had some health problems, which kind of changed everything at home. I had to step up a lot more, which I was completely fine with! I mean, she's my wife, and I want to be there for her, so I really shouldn't be complaining. I just... I guess I haven't really bounced back to my normal self since then. 

I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come in. I probably should have handled it better and come to see you sooner, right?
Have you noticed any decrease in pleasure from activities that you normally enjoy?

I know I mentioned this a little bit already, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much... but yeah, I guess that's exactly it. I just... I don't get that same spark from things anymore. 

Like I said, my fishing gear is just gathering dust out there, and the woodshop... well, I used to love spending hours in there, but now I just look at it and feel tired. And the chess with the kids... I mean, they're great kids, they really are, and I feel awful saying this, but I'm just faking it for them. I'm not actually enjoying it. I just sit there and move the pieces. 

Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm giving you the right information. I just feel so bad that I can't even enjoy spending time with my own family right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep?

Well, um... my sleep hasn't been the greatest, I suppose. I mean, I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes, especially when they're busy, so I'm sure it's nothing too out of the ordinary. 

But, uh, I can get into bed just completely exhausted after a long day at the site, and... I either just lie there running through all the bills and work schedules in my head, or I'll fall asleep and then wake up around three or four in the morning. And then I just kind of stare at the ceiling until it's time to drive to work. 

I'm probably just letting the stress get to me too much, right? I know I should be managing it better so I can be well-rested for my family and my crew. I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for?
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things that you wouldn't normally feel that way about?

Well, um... I mean, I know I shouldn't think this way, and I really hope this doesn't make me sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty awful about myself lately. 

It just feels like I'm letting everyone down. Like I've failed my wife by not being the rock she needs right now, and I'm failing the kids because I'm just going through the motions with them. And at work... I don't know, it's like every little thing that goes wrong on the site—if we go over budget on materials, or if someone misses a shift, or even just a minor safety hiccup—I just take it so personally. I keep thinking it's all my fault, like it's proof that I'm completely useless. 

Sometimes I even catch myself thinking that they'd all just be better off if I wasn't the one in charge anymore. I know that's probably a terrible thing to say, and I really should be stronger than this. I'm trying to push through it, I promise. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting to normal work stress.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying lately?

Oh, um... I mean... I know that's a really important question, and I want to be completely honest with you. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything, or that I'm, you know, going to do something terrible. I know I have a family depending on me. 

But... well, sometimes, on those early drives to the site before anyone else is awake... it's just so quiet, and I'm so tired. I catch myself thinking that maybe it would just be easier if I didn't make it there. Like if something just happened. 

And sometimes... I hope this doesn't sound too awful, but sometimes the thought of just steering off the road crosses my mind. It actually scares me, because it feels a little too close, you know? Like the thought is just sitting right there. 

I would never want to put my family through that, I promise. I know it's a terrible way to think. I'm just so exhausted. Does that... I mean, is that something people with stress go through? I hope I'm not alarming you too much.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I know I need to keep my strength up for the crew and everything, so I really do try to eat. I don't want you to think I'm just starving myself on purpose or anything like that. 

But, uh, lately... I don't know, it's just like food doesn't really have any taste anymore? It's almost like chewing on cardboard most days. So I guess I have been skipping breakfast before heading to the site, and even when I get home after a long shift, I just kind of pick at my dinner. My wife made my favorite roast last week and I barely touched it, which made me feel terrible because she worked hard on it. 

And, well, I guess my belt has had to come in a couple of notches recently, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. I'm sure it's just the stress of the job, right? Like my body is just running on adrenaline? I hope it's okay that I haven't been eating as much as I should be. I'm really trying to do better with it, I promise.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless and fidgety more often than usual?

Um, well... I mean, I don't think so? I really try to keep my energy up, you know, especially on the site. You can't really afford to be slow when you're managing a crew. 

I guess... I mean, my wife did mention the other day that I seem a little sluggish getting out of my chair in the evenings, but I'm pretty sure that's just because I've been on my feet all day. And as for being fidgety... no, I don't think I've been pacing around or anything like that. I really try to keep it together and stay steady for everyone else. 

I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I haven't noticed anything too out of the ordinary with how I'm moving. Is it normal to just feel kind of heavy from being tired? I don't want to give you the wrong impression or anything.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I know you just asked about that. I hope I didn't give a confusing answer a second ago, I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, yeah, just to be completely clear... no, I really don't think I'm moving any slower. I mean, aside from just the regular soreness from walking the concrete all day, I really try to keep my normal pace. I wouldn't want the crew to think I'm slacking off or getting lazy on them, you know? So I make a point to keep moving like I always do. 

Does that... I hope that makes sense? I just want to be as accurate as I can for you, so please let me know if I'm not answering these right.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I know we kind of just touched on that a second ago, too. I really hope I'm not frustrating you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But, uh, no... no trouble sitting still. Honestly, once I get home from the site and sit down in my chair, I pretty much just stay put for the rest of the night. I definitely don't feel jittery or like I need to pace around or anything like that. I mostly just try to stay quiet and rest up so I can be ready and focused for the guys the next day. 

Does that answer the question okay? I can try to think a little harder about it if you need me to, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt better for at least a couple of months?

Um, well... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything, because I know a lot of people have it worse. But, uh... no, not really. 

It's, um... it's been pretty constant for a while now. I'd say maybe... gosh, about a year and seven months? That's, um, that's when my wife started having some health problems, and it just kind of changed how everything worked at home. I really try to keep a positive attitude about it, you know, for her sake and for the guys at work, but it's just been a long stretch without much of a break from feeling this way. 

I hope it's okay to say that? I don't want to sound like I'm not trying to get better or anything, I just... I haven't really had a couple of good months in a row since all that started. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely back to your normal self?

Oh, um... I know this is going to sound almost exactly like what I just said, and I'm really sorry if I'm being repetitive. I definitely don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just being difficult for you... 

But, uh, no. I haven't really felt completely like my old self at all. I mean, I try really hard to act like it, you know? I put on a good face for the crew so they don't worry, and I try to be strong for my wife, so maybe from the outside it looks like I'm back to normal sometimes. But on the inside... no, it's just been that same heavy feeling this whole time. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a better answer for you. I really am trying my absolute best to push through it and get back to normal, I promise. Is... is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling fidgety or having an inability to sit still when you're at home or not working?

Oh, um... I feel terrible, I know you asked me something really similar just a few minutes ago. I'm so sorry, I hope I'm not making you go in circles or anything. I know your time is valuable. 

But, um, no... no fidgeting or anything like that. Like I mentioned, once I'm home, I really just sink into my chair and stay there. I don't have that nervous energy where I need to be moving around or tapping my foot or anything. I just try to stay as still and quiet as I can so I don't bother my wife while she's resting. 

I hope it's okay that my answer is basically the same as before? I just want to be completely honest with you and make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I... am I doing okay with these questions?
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain over the past year and a half?

Um, well... I, uh, I hope I'm not making it sound like I don't take care of myself. I know how important it is to keep my strength up, especially being out on the job sites and needing to help out around the house. I really do try to eat right, I promise.

But, um... I guess I have lost a little bit of weight. Not on purpose, really. It's just... lately, most days, food just kind of tastes like cardboard to me. So I'll, you know, I'll end up skipping breakfast, and then I just sort of pick at my dinner, even if I've been working hard all day. I just don't have the appetite for it. I did notice I had to bring my belt in a couple of notches recently, so I guess I have dropped some pounds. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or like I'm not trying to stay healthy. I just... eating feels like such a chore right now. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm in addition to thoughts of death?

Oh, um... gosh. I really, really don't want you to think I'm... you know, crazy, or a danger or anything. I promise I'm not. I know I have responsibilities to my guys at the site and to my wife, and I would never want to let them down or do anything selfish. 

But, um... well, if I'm being completely honest with you... sometimes on those really early drives, you know, before anyone else is even awake... I catch myself thinking that it would just be so much easier if I didn't make it there. 

And... I'm sorry, I'm a little ashamed to even say this out loud, but... sometimes the thought of just steering off the road... it scares me, because it feels a little too close. Like the thought is just right there and it wouldn't take much. But I always pull it together and keep driving, I swear. I try really hard to push those thoughts away. 

I hope... I hope that doesn't make you think less of me, or think I'm completely losing my grip. Is it... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than others or having trouble keeping up with your daily activities?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best to keep up, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm slacking off at work or leaving my wife to handle everything at home. I know I have to pull my weight, and I really do push myself to get things done.

But, um... I guess if I'm being totally honest, it has felt a little harder lately. I wouldn't say I'm moving in slow motion or anything dramatic like that. It's just... maybe it takes me a little longer to get going in the morning, or I feel a bit more sluggish when I'm walking the job site. I try really hard to hide it so the guys don't notice, because I need to set a good example for them. 

I'm still getting my work done, though. I make sure of that. I just... I guess I feel a little weighed down, maybe? I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy. I really am trying my best to stay on top of things. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were significantly worse than they are now?

Um, well... I really try to keep things steady, you know? I don't want to be one of those guys who's all over the place, making life difficult for my wife or my crew. I try to just keep my head down and push through. 

So, um... I don't think so? I mean, it's been pretty much like this for a while now. Just... this sort of heavy feeling, day in and day out. I haven't really noticed any times where it suddenly got a whole lot worse or anything like that. It's just kind of a constant thing I've been dealing with. 

I hope that's okay to say. I know sometimes people have, like, really dramatic crashes or something, and I don't want you to think I'm not taking this seriously because I don't have that. I'm just trying to give you the most accurate picture I can. Is that... is that helpful at all?
Have you experienced any periods where you felt nearly normal, but then your symptoms got significantly worse?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really don't want to waste your time or make it seem like I'm, you know, holding back information or anything. I just... I haven't really had any days where I felt totally normal, not for a long time. 

It's just been this same kind of... low, heavy feeling. It hasn't really bounced back up to normal and then crashed down again. I just kind of wake up every day and it's... it's just there. I really hope I'm explaining this right. I know you're trying to figure this out, and I want to be as helpful as I can. I just haven't had any of those good periods to tell you about, I'm sorry. Does that make sense?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely back to your normal self for at least two weeks?

Um... no, I haven't. I'm sorry, I know you've asked a few different ways now, and I really wish I could give you a better answer. I don't want to be difficult or make it seem like I'm not trying to get better. 

I just... I really can't remember a time in the last couple of years where I felt like my old self for that long. Maybe a day here or there where I forced myself to put on a good face for a family barbecue or something, but... not two whole weeks of actually feeling normal. It's just been this same kind of slog. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a better update for you on that. I'm really trying to be as honest as I can so you have what you need. Is it... is it bad that it's been that long?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely unable to work or take care of your daily responsibilities?

Um, well... I really try not to let things slip, you know? I've always prided myself on being reliable. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been getting harder. 

I wouldn't say I've been completely unable to work, I'm still showing up every day. But... I've started missing things. Just small details at first, but in my line of work, missing things can affect deadlines, and... well, safety. There was a near-miss recently, and... I just couldn't pretend it was just normal stress anymore. That really scared me. I don't want anyone getting hurt because I'm not on my game. 

And at home... I'm there physically, you know? I'm sitting on the couch. But my wife and kids... I think they're having to work around me a lot more lately, instead of being able to count on me the way they used to. I hate that I'm letting them down. 

I really hope I'm not sounding like I'm just making excuses or whining. I know I need to do better, and I want to. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
